# Switching Loops

- Previously, MD5 had the radial loop on from the start of the ramp to the end of the cycle
- I wanted to turn this off, because I suspect the radial loop is coupling the tune to the dipole hysteresis by way of the chromaticity (see [[13-08-2026 MD - Tune Drifts]]).
- Arthur Spierer helped to switch the synchro-loop on at flat-top.
- These are the timings (RF APP ALL 0.23.2 -> Modules -> Add Timing -> Timing tab): ![[Pasted image 20260820165031.png]]
- Seeing as we enabled the synchro-loop right at the start of the FT, I can't measure both the compensated and uncompensated scenarios in the same cycle anymore, because if I ramp BHYS there isn't any section of the FT with the synchro-loop on, the kick on, and no BHYS
- These settings were toggled (screenshot shows them in synchro-loop mode):![[Pasted image 20260820165421.png]]
	- Other settings touched were Then SpsLowLevelRF/B and SpSRfLoops/SynchroQ#phase 
	- Will revert all these at the end of the MD for cleanliness
- We still had a pretty good radial error of only about 0.1mm, with a max excursion of about 0.6mm when the switch from radial to synchro happens (from BCMega Drive):![[Pasted image 20260820170417.png]]
# Compensator Mystery

- Compensator might not have been incorporating correctly
One log:
```
2026-08-20 13:18:09,946 - ucap_hysterpid.converters.hyst_compensation - INFO -  
Measured B: 1.815551996231079 T  
B + BHYS = total B: 1.8000e+00 + -8.4434e-05 = 1.7999096043973088 T  
Working point B override: 1.81565 T  
---  
delta B x correction factor = BHYS change: 9.8004e-05 x 0.7 = 6.86026382446192e-05  
BHYS change after checks and thresholds: 6.86026382446192e-05 T  
New B + BHYS = total B: 1.8000e+00 + -1.5831e-05 = 1.7999782070355534 T
```
Next log:
```
2026-08-20 13:19:11,147 - ucap_hysterpid.converters.hyst_compensation - INFO -  
Measured B: 1.8154748678207397 T  
B + BHYS = total B: 1.8000e+00 + -1.3741e-04 = 1.7998566280561696 T  
Working point B override: 1.81565 T  
---  
delta B x correction factor = BHYS change: 1.7513e-04 x 0.7 = 0.00012259252548216804  
BHYS change after checks and thresholds: 0.00012259252548216804 T  
New B + BHYS = total B: 1.8000e+00 + -1.4818e-05 = 1.7999792205816518 T
```

- The BHYS at the end of the first log (-1.5831e-05) doesn't match the BHYS at the start of the next log (-1.3741e-4). 
- The LSA logs show that BHYS was not set to -1.5831e-05. Right after that log it was about -1.364e-4. By the time of the second log, it was indeed -1.3741e-04.
- The BHYS at the start of the first log is indeed correct.
- Where does this -1.3741e-4 come from? 

The actor log looks okay: 
```
2026-08-20 13:18:11,214 - cern.ucap.actions.standard.lsa.LsaTrimAction - INFO - Trim complete on MD_SHiP_L1230_Q26_S33_2026_LowInt: 5 settings updated, 1 settings sent to hardware.
```

- Mystery solved: BHYS had a non-zero 'correction'. My best guess for how this happened is that when I reset the 'value' via LSA to 0, it added a correction equal to -1 times the target (this is indeed how I found the settings).

# Email to Group

Hi everyone,

  

This is a summary of the synchro-loop/tune drift MD done on the 20th of August.

  

Previously (on the 13th), we had investigated how the tune drifts after a supercycle change. It looked like the tune drift followed the hysteretic drift of the flat-top dipole field, which raised eyebrows since these shouldn't be coupled. My suspicion was that this was an effect from the radial loop: the dipole field changes which causes a drift in orbit, then the radial loop changes the beam momentum to restore that orbit, and then change in beam momentum changes the tune via the chromaticity. More information on that [here](https://bdh-cern.github.io/hysteresis-notebook/MDs/2026/13-08-2026-MD---Tune-Drifts "https://bdh-cern.github.io/hysteresis-notebook/MDs/2026/13-08-2026-MD---Tune-Drifts").

  

In order to test this hypothesis, on the 20th we experimented with turning off the radial loop on the flat-top of our measurement cycle. This means that we were instead running on the synchro-loop at the flat-top. We then switched between SFT-production-like and LHC-filling-like supercycles, and observed how the tune drifted over multiple cycles. Of course, since we used protons, we weren't able to extract.

  

During the MD I also activated my dipole compensator, which pins the flat-top dipole field to a target value. However, I only activated it late along the flat-top, which allows us to see the reaction of the tune both with and without compensation.

  

In the plot below, the top axis shows the flat-top dipole field, in both the uncompensated (blue) and compensated (purples) regions. The axis below that shows QH in each region (red and orange, respectively). Note that since these are measured at different points along the FT, there is some natural variation even when there isn't any hysteresis or compensation. The next axis is the current on the MBIs (magenta), the shape of which is a result of the action of the compensator. The very bottom axis shows the supercycle type, with vertical, dashed lines showing the points at which they changed. Bear in mind that each point represents one SFTPRO1 cycle (NB: we actually used a SHiP cycle for the measurement, but these are equivalent for this purpose).

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)    

  

We can see that even with the synchro-loop on, the uncompensated QH follows the shape of the dipole drift (the blue and red lines). This is surprising to me and will require extra analysis of the orbits before I feel confident making any solid statements about it. However, we can see that the compensated QH appears to be restored to a reasonable value by the action of the compensator. This was not the case when looking at the same scenario with the radial loop on the 13th, in which case the compensator appeared to kill the tune drift, but it stabilised at the wrong value (0.002 difference to the target).

  

Ultimately, this is a good data-point since it shows we may be able to correct the spill with only a dipole trim, but that this probably relies on using the synchro-loop at FT. Personally, I don't know how viable this is, but I would be interested to hear any thoughts on how/if this could work operationally.

  

Thanks to Arthur for setting up this cycle to work with the synchro-loop, and as usual to the operators and Theo for playing the SC changes!

  

Best,

  

Brendan
